title: What are Templates?
description: Separate your HTML from Python logic using Django’s template system.

slides.title: Why Templates? 🧩
slides.content:
# Separation of Concerns Mixing HTML directly in Python code (like `return HttpResponse("

Hello

")`) is messy and hard to maintain. **Templates** allow you to keep your frontend (HTML) separate from your backend (Python). - Templates are files (usually `.html`) that contain static markup plus special **template syntax** for dynamic content. - Django’s template engine processes these files, injects data from your views, and returns a final HTML page.

quizData.question: What is the main benefit of using templates?

options.text: They make your code run faster
They separate HTML from Python logic
They replace the need for views

quizData.explanation: Templates allow you to keep presentation separate from business logic, making your code cleaner and more maintainable.

slides.title: Where Templates Live 📁
slides.content:
By default, Django looks for templates in a folder named `templates` inside each app. You can also configure global template directories in `settings.py`.

```
myapp/
    templates/
        myapp/
            home.html   # namespacing prevents conflicts
```

**Namespacing** (putting templates in an app‑named subfolder) is a good practice to avoid name collisions between apps.
